== Biography ==
=== Jane Dysart: proposed father replacement, 23 October 2026 ===

[[Glasglow-11|Jane Catherine (Glasglow) Dysart]] is assessed as daughter of [[Glasgow-4090|John Glasgow, farmer]] at 92% confident inference, replacing the inherited [[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow]] father attachment. Jane’s identity is anchored by [[Glasgow-4070|Nancy Glasgow]]’s express niece Margaret Kennedy, the Rasharkin baptism naming Margaret’s mother Jane Glascaw, and James Dysart’s 1881 will naming daughter Margaret Kennedy, son Robert and granddaughter Mary Anne McCaughern. The 1892 probate citation coherently identifies Jane Dysart’s wider child group. Mary Anne’s appearance as a witness at [[Glasgow-1371|Ann Glasgow]]’s 1875 marriage independently links the Dysart descendants to [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]]’s household. That John’s 1846 marriage names father [[Glasgow-4090|John Glasgow, farmer]]. The combined kinship, recorded Glasgow birth surnames, compatible generations and matched households support the same record-defined father for Jane at 92% confident inference, replacing the unsupported older-Alexander pedigree. No inspected record directly names Jane’s father. The citation is incomplete and is not an adjudicated pedigree; the underlying petition and heir schedule remain uninspected. [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]]’s Ballydonnelly description and Lizzie remain unresolved. The witness association supports the family network but does not by itself prove kinship. A maternal half-sibling explanation involving different Glasgow fathers remains possible, without positive evidence favoring it. [[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow]] is chronologically compatible and retained as an unselected alternative, rather than declared impossible. This subjective percentage assesses Jane’s father as the record-defined John Glasgow, farmer, named in [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow]]’s 1846 marriage. It does not identify the 1796 Desertoghill flax grower or establish John’s proposed Larne ancestry. [[Unknown-761034|Rosanna]] remains Jane’s separately unproved maternal attachment; this replacement does not identify John’s wife or prove a John–Rosanna marriage. Jane’s life dates and all existing relatives apart from the selected father are preserved.

Jane was born about 1804.  She passed away in 1868.

</ref>

Jane died at Crushybracken, Rasharkin parish, County Antrim, on 13 September 1868, aged 64. The civil register describes her as married and "the wife of a farmer", and records the cause of death as heart disease of two years' duration, certified. Her husband [[Dysart-1684|James Dysart]], who signed by his mark as "James Dysert", was present at her death at Crushybracken; the death was registered on 22 September 1868.<ref name="JaneDeathGRONI">General Register Office for Northern Ireland, death register, Ballymena superintendent registrar's district, Clough registrar's district, entry 418, 13 September 1868: Jane Dysert, Crushybracken, Rasharkin parish, female, married, 64, the wife of a farmer; cause disease of the heart, two years, certified; informant James Dysert (his mark), present at death, Crushybracken; registered 22 September 1868. Registration number D/1868/22/1004/1/418. Image viewed at [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/ GRONI online], 23 September 2026.</ref>
